title: An Unexpected Battle Over Banning Caste Discrimination

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代，我还在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏去工作，然后你会把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的活生生的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: California is about to become the first state in the country to outlaw discrimination based on a person's caste.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州即将成为全美第一个立法禁止基于种姓制度进行歧视的州。

sentences.en: My colleague, Amy Chin, on why so many now believe a prejudice that originated on the other side of the globe now requires legal protection in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的同事艾米·秦将讲述为什么现在有这么多人认为，这种起源于地球另一端的偏见，如今在美国也需要法律保护。

sentences.en: and why so many are equally convinced that it's a bad idea that will backfire.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么同样有许多人坚信这是一个会适得其反的坏主意。

sentences.en: It's Monday, September 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月25日，星期一。

sentences.en: Amy, I wonder if you can tell us about this piece of legislation which was recently passed by California's democratically controlled legislature
sentences.zh: 艾米，我想请你介绍一下这项最近由加州民主党控制的立法机构通过的法案，

sentences.en: and now sits on the desk of its Democratic governor,
sentences.zh: 它现在正摆在民主党州长

sentences.en: Gavin Newsom.
sentences.zh: 加文·纽森的办公桌上。

sentences.en: So the bill is called Senate Bill 403 or SB 403 for short, and essentially it will make caste discrimination illegal in California.
sentences.zh: 这项法案被称为参议院第403号法案，简称SB 403，本质上它将使加州的种姓歧视成为非法行为。

sentences.en: And that means everywhere from housing to employment, discrimination based on caste will not be allowed.
sentences.zh: 这意味着从住房到就业，所有领域都将禁止基于种姓的歧视。

sentences.en: It will become a protected characteristic just like sex, gender, sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 它将成为像性别、性取向一样的受保护特征。

sentences.en: People will not be able to discriminate on that basis.
sentences.zh: 人们将不能再以此为由进行歧视。

sentences.en: So just define this word, caste.
sentences.zh: 那么，请解释一下“种姓”这个词。

sentences.en: I think we all have a little bit of a sense of what it means, but would benefit from hearing you explain it.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大家都对它的含义有一点了解，但如果能听你解释一下会更好。

sentences.en: So the caste system is one of the oldest systems of social stratification, and it began in India thousands of years ago.
sentences.zh: 种姓制度是最古老的社会分层制度之一，起源于几千年前的印度。

sentences.en: It has its roots in Hinduism, and essentially it's a rigid social hierarchy that people are born into.
sentences.zh: 它植根于印度教，本质上是一种人们与生俱来的僵化社会等级制度。

sentences.en: And the system really governed everything about people's lives, from who they married to the job that they did.
sentences.zh: 这个制度实际上支配了人们生活的方方面面，从婚嫁对象到所从事的工作。

sentences.en: And at a very basic level, you have at the top of this hierarchy, the Brahmins, who historically were priests.
sentences.zh: 在最基础的层面上，这个等级制度的顶端是婆罗门，他们历史上是祭司。

sentences.en: They had access to education and were considered the pureSt.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有受教育的机会，被认为是最纯洁的。

sentences.en: Then you have the warrior caste, the merchant caste, the laborer caste.
sentences.zh: 然后是武士种姓、商人种姓和劳工种姓。

sentences.en: And at the very bottom, you had what were known as the quote-unquote untouchables, who prefer to call themselves Dalits.
sentences.zh: 而在最底层，是所谓的“不可接触者”，他们更愿意称自己为达利特。

sentences.en: And they were considered to be so impure that they were outcasts.
sentences.zh: 他们被认为极其不洁，是社会弃儿。

sentences.en: And they were relegated to doing jobs that were also seen as impure, like street sweeping or toilet cleaning.
sentences.zh: 他们被降级从事同样被视为不洁的工作，比如扫街或清理厕所。

sentences.en: And they couldn't even drink from the same well water as other castes.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不能和其他种姓的人共用一口水井。

sentences.en: Over time, the system spread throughout South Asia and spread to other religious communities, like to Christians and Sikhs.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这种制度传播到整个南亚，并扩散到其他宗教群体，如基督徒和锡克教徒。

sentences.en: And the caste hierarchy was also reinforced under British colonial rule.
sentences.zh: 在英国殖民统治下，种姓等级制度也得到了强化。

sentences.en: And then, in the mid-20th century, caste discrimination was outlawed in countries like India and Nepal.
sentences.zh: 后来，在20世纪中期，印度和尼泊尔等国宣布种姓歧视非法。

sentences.en: But, of course, we know that just because you ban something on paper doesn't mean it actually is gone in practice.
sentences.zh: 但我们当然知道，仅仅在纸面上禁止某事，并不意味着它在实践中真正消失了。

sentences.en: And so caste is still a very strong marker of identity in many places.
sentences.zh: 因此，种姓在许多地方仍然是一个非常强烈的身份标签。

sentences.en: And you can see it in the privileges that people have, in their social circles, in the kinds of opportunities that they have access to.
sentences.zh: 你可以从人们享有的特权、社交圈以及他们所能获得的机会中看到这一点。

sentences.en: And this is really still present across South Asia.
sentences.zh: 这在整个南亚依然存在。

sentences.en: Much in the way, I imagine that when racial prejudice in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想，这很像美国在种族偏见

sentences.en: is outlawed, it nevertheless keeps happening.
sentences.zh: 被法律禁止后，却依然不断发生的情况。

sentences.en: Just because it's baned in the law doesn't mean it doesn't persiSt.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为法律禁止，并不意味着它不会持续存在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And some people have drawn that parallel.
sentences.zh: 有些人也做过这种类比。

sentences.en: The journalist Isabel Wilkerson wrote a best-selling book called Caste, in which she compared the caste system in India to the way that race operates in America.
sentences.zh: 记者伊莎贝尔·威尔克森写了一本畅销书《种姓》，她在书中将印度的种姓制度与美国的种族运作方式进行了比较。

sentences.en: The idea that you can be born into a certain hierarchy and that it can be extremely difficult to escape your circumstances.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，你可能生来就处于某种等级制度中，而要摆脱你的处境可能极其困难。

sentences.en: So the fact, Amy, that there's a bill in California about caste discrimination now suggests that lawmakers there believe that this is not just something
sentences.zh: 那么艾米，加州现在出现了一项关于种姓歧视的法案，这是否意味着那里的立法者认为这不仅仅是

sentences.en: that remains a problem overseas in South Asia, but it has somehow been imported into the United States.
sentences.zh: 一个在海外南亚地区存在的问题，而是它已经以某种方式被引入了美国？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They've been hearing from their constituents in California that this is becoming a bigger and bigger problem in the diaspora and that in order to protect residents of California,
sentences.zh: 他们一直从加州的选民那里听到，这在侨民群体中正成为一个越来越严重的问题，为了保护加州居民，

sentences.en: they need to have a bill specifically focusing on caste discrimination in order to prevent this type of discrimination from happening in the future.
sentences.zh: 他们需要一项专门针对种姓歧视的法案，以防止这种歧视在未来发生。

sentences.en: But why right now?
sentences.zh: 但为什么是现在？

sentences.en: I mean, you just referred to a diaspora.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你刚才提到了侨民。

sentences.en: People from South Asia have been coming to California for generations.
sentences.zh: 来自南亚的人们几代人以来一直来到加州。

sentences.en: Why this moment for this bill to resolve this problem?
sentences.zh: 为什么偏偏在这个时候提出这项法案来解决这个问题？

sentences.en: So it really has to do with patterns of immigration.
sentences.zh: 这确实与移民模式有关。

sentences.en: After a big Immigration Act in 1965 was passed in the United States, we saw a huge migration of people from Asia, including India, to the United States.
sentences.zh: 在1965年美国通过一项重大移民法案后，我们看到了大量来自亚洲（包括印度）的人移民到美国。

sentences.en: And a lot of those people that came over were people who were skilled workers.
sentences.zh: 很多过来的人都是技术工人。

sentences.en: They had degrees and were able to get jobs in the tech industry and the medical industry in the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有学位，能够在美国的科技行业和医疗行业找到工作。

sentences.en: And a lot of these people in India who were able to have the resources to get these types of degrees were from the upper caste.
sentences.zh: 而在印度，很多有资源获得这些学位的人都来自高种姓。

sentences.en: And so for a long time, caste discrimination didn't really exist, or at least people didn't think it really existed because everyone was from the same caste.
sentences.zh: 所以很长一段时间里，种姓歧视并不真正存在，或者至少人们认为它不存在，因为大家都是同一个种姓。

sentences.en: But that's changed over time as the composition of the people who are coming from India has also changed.
sentences.zh: 但随着来自印度的人员构成发生变化，这种情况也随之改变了。

sentences.en: In large part, that has to do with certain changes that are happening in India itself.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上，这与印度国内发生的一些变化有关。

sentences.en: The country has put in place a system of essentially affirmative action where there are quotas now for people from lower castes to go to universities,
sentences.zh: 该国实施了一套本质上的平权行动制度，现在为低种姓人群进入大学、

sentences.en: to occupy government positions.
sentences.zh: 担任政府职位设定了配额。

sentences.en: And we are now starting to see the effects of those affirmative action policies where you had a lot of people who were from lower caste going to these universities
sentences.zh: 我们现在开始看到这些平权政策的效果，很多低种姓的人进入了这些大学，

sentences.en: and now they suddenly have the degrees to get those skilled worker visas to come to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在他们突然有了获得技术工人签证来到美国的学位。

sentences.en: And so the people who are coming over from India to the United States are actually much more diverse.
sentences.zh: 所以从印度来到美国的人实际上更加多元化了。

sentences.en: And in California, we've really seen that shift happen because a lot of these people are coming to work in IT jobs, specifically in Silicon Valley,
sentences.zh: 在加州，我们确实看到了这种转变，因为这些人中有许多是来从事IT工作的，特别是在硅谷，

sentences.en: which is why we're seeing so much of this issue being debated in California now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们现在在加州看到这么多关于这个问题的辩论。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So suddenly a much more diverse group of South Asians are in a place like California.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，一群更多元化的南亚人来到了像加州这样的地方。

sentences.en: And I'm going to guess that that creates a greater opportunity for potential conflict once they arrive.
sentences.zh: 我猜这会给他们抵达后带来更大的潜在冲突机会。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the caste issue really burst into public consciousness in 2020 when California brought a lawsuit against Cisco, which is a pretty well-known tech company.
sentences.zh: 种姓问题在2020年真正进入公众视野，当时加州对思科公司提起诉讼，这是一家相当知名的科技公司。

sentences.en: And in the lawsuit, an employee who is from a Dalit background accused two of his bosses, who are from upper caste backgrounds, of discriminating against him
sentences.zh: 在诉讼中，一名达利特背景的员工指控他的两名高种姓背景的上司对他进行歧视，

sentences.en: in his job on the basis of caste.
sentences.zh: 在工作中基于种姓对他进行歧视。

sentences.en: He said that they had given him less pay, that they had denied certain opportunities to him in the workplace, and the state on his behalf was suing Cisco.
sentences.zh: 他说他们降低了他的工资，在职场中拒绝给他某些机会，州政府代表他起诉了思科。

sentences.en: And this really led to a huge conversation in California, I think, in a way that we hadn't seen before.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在加州引发了一场前所未有的巨大讨论。

sentences.en: And this was taking place at around the same time as the death of George Floyd had sparked the Black Lives Matter movement, and suddenly people were able
sentences.zh: 这发生的时间点大约与乔治·弗洛伊德之死引发“黑人的命也是命”运动的时间重合，突然之间人们能够

sentences.en: to describe their experiences with caste discrimination using vocabulary that was understandable to people who understood it in the context of race.
sentences.zh: 用那些在种族背景下能被理解的词汇来描述他们经历的种姓歧视。

sentences.en: Terms like systemic discrimination and oppressed communities.
sentences.zh: 诸如系统性歧视和受压迫群体之类的术语。

sentences.en: These were all concepts that now the public was much more familiar with.
sentences.zh: 这些都是公众现在非常熟悉的概念。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: So the conversation going on in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，在美国

sentences.en: in the wake of George Floyd's death, this wrenching conversation about race, oppression, systemic racism, that is giving people from South Asia a framework for thinking about
sentences.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德去世后，关于种族、压迫、系统性种族主义的痛苦讨论，正在为南亚人提供一个思考框架，

sentences.en: the discrimination that they believe they are experiencing here in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 思考他们认为自己在美国经历的歧视，

sentences.en: that's been imported from South Asia.
sentences.zh: 这些歧视是从南亚引入的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it's around this time that people started to feel more comfortable talking about their experiences with caste discrimination.
sentences.zh: 也正是在这个时候，人们开始感到更自在地谈论他们经历的种姓歧视。

sentences.en: I mean, we heard stories about people experiencing wage theft at the hands of their upper caste bosses.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们听到了关于人们在高种姓老板手下遭受工资克扣的故事。

sentences.en: There were people talking about social exclusion, that they weren't being allowed to eat from the same cups and plates as Brahmin employers.
sentences.zh: 有人谈论社会排斥，说他们不被允许与婆罗门雇主共用杯子和盘子。

sentences.en: I spoke with one doctor in California who said that when other doctors in her city had found out that she was from a lower caste, they stopped referring patients to her practice.
sentences.zh: 我采访了加州的一位医生，她说当她所在城市的其他医生发现她来自低种姓时，他们就停止向她的诊所转诊病人了。

sentences.en: And one person that I spoke to really stood out to me.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一个人让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: His name was
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫

sentences.en: Bim Narayan Bishwakarma.
sentences.zh: 比姆·纳拉扬·比什瓦卡马。
zh_words: 比姆·纳拉扬·比什瓦卡马

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, Bim.
sentences.zh: 你好，比姆。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: He's 44.
sentences.zh: 他今年44岁。

sentences.en: He works at a convenience store in El Cerrito, California.
sentences.zh: 他在加州埃尔塞里托的一家便利店工作。

sentences.en: And he's from Nepal originally.
sentences.zh: 他最初来自尼泊尔。

sentences.en: And he told me that he had experienced caste-based discrimination growing up in Nepal.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他在尼泊尔长大时经历过基于种姓的歧视。

sentences.en: While growing as a child, I was not that much respected, especially when it comes to, you know, entering friends' houses.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，我没有得到太多的尊重，特别是在进入朋友家的时候。

sentences.en: When he would hang out with his friends, his friends' parents wouldn't let him go into their homes because he was from a lower caste.
sentences.zh: 当他和朋友出去玩时，朋友的父母不让他进屋，因为他来自低种姓。

sentences.en: And I used to feel like, oh, I felt like insulted, discriminated.
sentences.zh: 我过去常觉得，哦，我觉得被侮辱了，被歧视了。

sentences.en: Discriminated.
sentences.zh: 被歧视。

sentences.en: So, of course, one of the reasons to come to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，来到美国的原因之一

sentences.en: is caste-based discrimination.
sentences.zh: 就是基于种姓的歧视。

sentences.en: And he eventually moved to California.
sentences.zh: 他最终搬到了加州。

sentences.en: He got a job.
sentences.zh: 他找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: And at one point, a few years ago, he was looking for a room in a shared house and he found a great one.
sentences.zh: 几年前，他曾在合租房里找房间，他找到了一个很棒的。

sentences.en: And on August 18, 2021,
I visited a house.
sentences.zh: 我参观了一所房子。

sentences.en: He spoke with the landlord who was also from Nepal.
sentences.zh: 他与房东交谈，房东也来自尼泊尔。

sentences.en: The landlord showed his contentment to welcome me as a tenant.
sentences.zh: 房东表示很高兴欢迎我作为租客。

sentences.en: The landlord was really excited for him to move in as a single guy.
sentences.zh: 房东对他作为一个单身汉搬进来感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: So, presumably, he would be, you know, quiet and not too much of a disturbance.
sentences.zh: 所以，大概他会很安静，不会造成太多干扰。

sentences.en: Everything was finalized.
sentences.zh: 一切都敲定了。

sentences.en: The landlord requested me the deposit to his account.
sentences.zh: 房东要求我把押金打到他的账户里。

sentences.en: So, he gives the landlord his deposit and everything seemed like it was fine.
sentences.zh: 于是，他把押金给了房东，一切看起来都很顺利。

sentences.en: But then, six hours later, he gets a call from the landlord and the landlord says, sorry, I can't rent this room to you anymore.
sentences.zh: 但六小时后，他接到了房东的电话，房东说，对不起，我不能再把这个房间租给你了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that was talking to me as I had a smooth and pleasant conversation with him and everything was finalized that day.
sentences.zh: 那天我和他进行了顺畅愉快的交谈，一切都敲定了，他却这样对我。

sentences.en: Then I asked him what happened and why he flipped over his words.
sentences.zh: 然后我问他发生了什么，为什么出尔反尔。

sentences.en: Beam said he was asking questions, you know, why?
sentences.zh: 比姆说他一直在问，你知道，为什么？

sentences.en: And the landlord was giving all kinds of reasons.
sentences.zh: 房东给了各种各样的理由。

sentences.en: He said he needs a room for family members who visit.
sentences.zh: 他说他需要留个房间给来访的家人。

sentences.en: And Beam was just very confused.
sentences.zh: 比姆感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, I suddenly remember the scene where we exchanged our numbers and I sang my name.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，我突然想起我们交换号码并告知姓名的场景。

sentences.en: He remembers that when he had given the deposit to the landlord, he had given him his full name.
sentences.zh: 他记得当他把押金交给房东时，他告诉了对方全名。

sentences.en: And his last name is Bishwakarma, which in Nepal is associated with a lower caste.
sentences.zh: 他的姓氏是比什瓦卡马，在尼泊尔与低种姓相关联。

sentences.en: And then Beam started to confront his landlord.
sentences.zh: 然后比姆开始质问他的房东。

sentences.en: I mean, I told him that, I know why you are denying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我告诉他，我知道你为什么拒绝。

sentences.en: I know the reason why you are denying the room to me.
sentences.zh: 我知道你拒绝把房间租给我的原因。
